description_full: CBRE Group, Inc. operates as a commercial real estate services and investment company in the United States, the United Kingdom, and internationally. The company operates through Advisory Services, Building Operations and Experience, Project Management, and Real Estate Investments segments. The Advisory Services segment offers strategic advice and execution to owners, investors, and occupiers of real estate in connection with leasing of offices, and industrial and retail space; clients fully integrated property sales services under the CBRE Capital Markets brand; clients commercial mortgage and structured financing services; originates and sells commercial mortgage loans; property management services, such as marketing, building engineering, lease administration, accounting, investment reporting services, financial services on a contractual basis for owners of and investors in office, industrial, and retail properties; and valuation services that include market value appraisals, litigation support, discounted cash flow analyses, and feasibility studies, as well as consulting services, such as property condition reports, hotel advisory, and environmental consulting. The Global Workplace Solutions segment provides facilities management, and project management services comprising building consulting, program, and project and cost management services under the Turner & Townsend brand name. The Real Estate Investments segment offers investment management services under the CBRE Investment Management brand to pension funds, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, foundations, endowments, and other institutional investors and development services, such as real estate development and investment activities under the Trammell Crow Company brand to users and investors in commercial real estate, and for their own account. CBRE Group, Inc. was founded in 1906 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas.

financial_summary: CBRE Group Inc is a large-cap real estate business with a $40.3B market cap on $40.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.9×.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 4% operating margin trails the Real Estate median (22%) by 18pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.22x its revenue share).
It accounts for 11.3% of sector revenue and 2.5% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 145 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 25% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 20% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 35% and a beta of 1.01, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $286.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 54% in the 2020 crash, 39% in the 2022 bear market and 90% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $104 (margin of safety -34%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 26%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $31.53 to $302 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Real Estate peers: EV/EBITDA 22.8 vs 16.3 and P/FCF 33.8 vs 17.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 38% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 12 covering analysts target $170 on average, 22% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 11% earns above the cost of capital of 9.0%, but the 2pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.20).
It converts 3% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.35x.
AFFO margin (a proxy for distributable REIT cash) is 3%.
ROE of 13% is amplified by 3.5x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 0.3% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.3x net debt to EBITDA ($1.9B of cash against $7.6B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 3.9x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.6% over 3 years, 11.2% over 5 years and 14.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 9% of profits supports about 1.0% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -5.3% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: deferred revenue up 19% and FFO growth of -3.2% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (0.9% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 14, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $1.4M sold).
It returns 2.4% a year to shareholders (2.4% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 2.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 155,000 employees, each generates about $262K of revenue, 0.1x the Real Estate median, and revenue has grown 14.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $8K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $5.3M (20x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
